english.title: Broadcast name / address / picture of the victim of a sexual offence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) during the lifetime of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) when an allegation had been made that an offence of **(..SPECIFY THE SEXUAL OFFENCE..) had been committed against

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

and being the

(C)_[body corporate providing a programme service, namely **(..SPECIFY PROGRAMME SERVICE..)]_
(D)_[person having functions in relation to the **(..SPECIFY PROGRAMME..) corresponding to those of an editor of a newspaper]_

included in the programme

(E)_[the name]_
(F)_[the address]_
(G)_[a still picture]_
(H)_[a moving picture]_

of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), being a matter likely to lead members of the public to identify **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) as the person against whom the offence was alleged to have been committed
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) and 5(1) of the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 1992.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
during lifetime of a person
when allegation had been made that a sexual offence
had been committed in respect of that person
being the body corporate providing a programme service or
a person having function relating to a programme corresponding to the editor of a newspaper
included in the programme
a name/address/still picture/moving picture
likely to lead members of public to identify that person as the victim

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Attorney General is required for prosecution.
(ii) See the list of relevant sexual offences to which this offence applies.
(iii) See also offence wordings: H4322, H4323 and H4324 - which relate to complainants in sex offences where someone has been accused.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
